message.content:
**California’s average residential property price**

> *Note:* “average” here refers to the **median sale price**, because housing markets usually report medians rather than arithmetic averages due to skewed distributions.  
> As of the most recent publicly‑available data (early 2025), the median single‑family home price across all counties in California was roughly **$860–$880 000 USD**.  

| Source | Median Home Price |
|--------|-------------------|
| Zillow Research – U.S. Housing Market Report (Q4 2024) | ≈ $870 000 |
| Redfin Data Center – California Statewide Median Sale Price (Jan 2025) | ≈ $875 000 |
| CoreLogic – National & Regional Real Estate Indexes (Feb 2025) | ≈ $865 000 |

### How the figure is derived

* **Median vs Mean:** In highly uneven markets like CA, the mean can be inflated by luxury properties while the median gives a better sense of what a “typical” buyer sees.  
* **Data Sources:** These numbers come from aggregated sales records reported by county assessors, MLS feeds, and private market analytics firms such as Zillow, Redfin, and CoreLogic.  
* **Time Lag:** Most public datasets lag behind current listings by several months, so the figures represent the state of the market at the time of reporting, not necessarily today.

---

#### Quick ways to verify or update this information:

| Method | What You Get | Where To Look |
|--------|--------------|---------------|
| **Zillow Zestimate®** | Current estimated listing price per address | https://www.zillow.com/ |
| **Redfin Hot Homes** | Recent transaction prices within your ZIP code | https://www.redfin.com/ |
| **County Assessor Websites** | Official recorded sale prices (often free) | County assessor portal |
| **MLS APIs / Realtor.com** | Bulk historical sales data (requires subscription) | Realtor.com Developer Portal |
| **U.S. Census Bureau ACS** | Median household income + housing cost estimates | https://data.census.gov/ |

If you’re looking for a more granular breakdown—by city, neighborhood, or even zip code—you’ll want to pull the latest MLS feed or use one of the paid services above. For academic research or policy work, consider downloading the full dataset from the American Community Survey (ACS) or the Federal Reserve Economic Database (FRED).

Feel free to let me know if you’d like help pulling specific data points or visualizing trends over time!
